note: P-B-2018-77238-4380ec81 (2018 MCM B, Team 77238): 23 pages, 50 measured regions, 18 figures and 19 grids recorded, 13 fragments excluded, no unaccounted region. The paper is a two-model chain - a language-development simulation and an office-siting model - and its exhibit language splits along that seam: the model half argues with schematics and two small grids, the solution half carries every dense exhibit (six 16-curve plates, three maps, four grouping grids), the sensitivity half is grids only, and the memo page ends on an uncaptioned map and a booktabs answer grid. Three structural traps worth carrying to the queue: the heading detector mistakes table rows for headings, so the section paths here come from the numbered headings only; the paper prints fifteen numbered tables but seven of them are native text that the region pass never boxes, so this record covers the twelve grids the detector measured plus the notation and memo blocks; and both page-break continuations arrive without their header, which is why they are recorded as separate exhibits with continued set.
rules: Caption side is decided by exhibit kind, not by available space: all 18 recorded figures carry their caption under the artwork and all 17 captioned grids carry it over the box, on every page of the paper, with no exception. The two uncaptioned exhibits - the notation grid and the memo's answer grid - sit under a heading that names them instead [caption.position].

Numbering is positional only: Figure N and Table N with a plain space, never a colon and never a full stop, across all 35 captions; figure and table numbers run independently and neither restarts, so the caption alone places an exhibit in the argument [caption.numbering].

Captions are noun phrases: not one of the 35 carries a finite verb, so voice is none throughout, and none states a unit, a condition, a parameter value or a conclusion. Figure captions run 5 to 16 words, grid captions 5 to 14, and the longest are the ones that have to say what is being compared - total number and rank, number of native speakers and rank [caption.voice].

Family follows the argument stage. The six model-kind exhibits are three box-and-arrow drawings, one rank-ordered point cloud, one axis-only interval strip and two grids; the twenty-two solution-kind exhibits are six 16-curve line plates, three maps, two more flowcharts, one node-link distance example, a second interval strip and eight grids; the five sensitivity exhibits are grids and nothing else; the memo closes on one map and one grid. No bar, histogram, heatmap, 3D view or colourbar appears anywhere in the paper [place.section_kind].

The recurring figure template is the sixteen-curve line plate: years on the x axis, 0 to N on the y axis in scientific notation without a unit, sixteen series keyed in a box inside the upper right corner, and a twin frame beside it turning the same run into rank 0-16 read top-down. Figures 6, 8 and 9 print that pair six times across three spreads, and the frames are measured as six regions because the ordinate scales differ [geometry.legend].

A panel plate carries one caption, printed once under the pair, and the second frame inherits it verbatim. The only plate whose key moves outside the artwork is the four-frame map row, where the sixteen-entry key sits in the right margin and each frame stamps its year in red underneath [geometry.panel_count].

Maps encode by bubble size plus the country name printed on the map, never by a legend box or a colourbar: the three office maps put one bubble on each office country, a dot on every grouped country and letter the office countries in place, so size carries almost nothing (bubble diameters vary only about 1.4 to 1) and the reader is meant to read names, not areas [geometry.colorbar].

Grid ruling is heavy by default: 17 of the 19 grids box every cell, and the tall ones draw eighteen horizontals at a 16.8 pt pitch plus every internal vertical. The memo's answer grid is the only booktabs block - three rules, no verticals - and Table 11 is the only half-drawn one: verticals only, open on the right and at the bottom. No grid uses zebra striping and no grid uses a diagonal header [table.rule_style].

Merged cells appear only where a label owns several body rows: the group number and the continent merge down the member rows of the two geographic grouping grids, the four GDP-level header cells each span two columns in the sensitivity summary, and the Asia and Europe stubs span two rows there. The two language-structure grouping grids merge nothing - their tall rows are single cells holding a stack of three languages [table.merged_cells].

Grid width tracks the column count, not the importance: the two-column memo grid and the four-column location grid run at 89 to 99 per cent of the text measure, the seven-column simulation grid at 94 per cent, the nine-column office strips at or past the measure, while the three grids holding one number per cell shrink to 62 to 73 per cent. Nothing in the paper is set landscape or rotated [table.width].

Units are almost never in the header: Table 2 prints Increased rate (%) over its column and is the only grid that does. Everywhere else - the GDP growth rates of Table 1, the three sensitivity sweeps - the per cent sign is repeated inside every cell, so the header row stays pure label [table.units_in_header].

Numbers are centred, never decimal-aligned and never right-aligned: the signed percentages of the three sensitivity grids and the counts of the grouping grids all sit on the cell centre, so digits do not line up in a column even where every entry is a decimal [table.decimal_aligned].

Header depth is one row in every grid, but the band is stretched wherever labels stack: the simulation grid doubles it to fit a pair label over its year, the birth-rate grid doubles it to fit Change of Net Birth Rate over the four levels, and the sensitivity summary needs two rows for its stacked corner. Below that band the pitch is uniform, which is what makes the eight-row body of Table 15 readable despite its rules being drawn in light grey [table.header_rows].

Two grids break across a page and neither repeats its header: the tail of the language-structure grouping arrives at the top of page 13 as three bare rows, and five language rows of the migration sweep arrive at the top of page 19 with the caption still on the page before. A continuation is therefore recognisable only by its column count and by the missing rule under its last row [table.continued].

Announcement is optional and mostly numberless: 14 of the 35 captioned exhibits get a lead-in sentence, 11 of those on the exhibit's own page, and only 8 of the 14 print the exhibit's number in the sentence. The other six say the following table, the table below, the following figure, or nothing at all, so the caption has to do the pointing [mention.lead_sentence].

Interpretation after the exhibit belongs to the sensitivity section: all three sweeps are followed by a paragraph that opens on the grid itself, whereas the solution grids are followed by the next step of the argument rather than by a reading of the grid [mention.trail_sentence].

Exhibits cluster away from the page top: only 14 of the 37 sit in the top third of their page, 10 in the middle and 13 in the bottom third, and no exhibit occupies a page alone - every one shares its page with text or with a second exhibit, which is why the papers' figures are read as inline evidence rather than as plates [place.page_zone].
